summary: Climbazole is a topical imidazole antifungal used chiefly as an anti-dandruff active and as a cosmetic preservative in shampoos and leave-on scalp products, typically at around 0.5-2% in the finished formulation. It acts against Malassezia (Pityrosporum) yeasts implicated in dandruff and seborrhoeic conditions. It is applied to the scalp/skin per the cosmetic product's instructions; there is no oral or systemic dosing. Systemic absorption from topical use is minimal. Climbazole is NOT FDA-approved as a drug; information here is drawn from non-FDA cosmetic-ingredient and EMA/SCCS (Scientific Committee on Consumer Safety)-type sources.

moa: Climbazole is an imidazole antifungal. Like other azoles, it inhibits fungal cytochrome P450-dependent 14-alpha-demethylase (lanosterol demethylase), blocking conversion of lanosterol to ergosterol. The resulting ergosterol depletion and accumulation of methylated sterol precursors disrupt the fungal cell membrane, inhibiting growth of Malassezia (Pityrosporum) yeasts that contribute to dandruff and seborrhoeic scalp conditions.

preg: No specific human safety data for climbazole in pregnancy. As a topical cosmetic ingredient, systemic absorption is minimal, so significant fetal exposure from normal use is unlikely. There is no systemic therapeutic indication; use cosmetic products as directed and seek medical advice for persistent scalp conditions.
lact: No specific lactation data. Systemic absorption from topical cosmetic use is minimal, so exposure via breast milk is expected to be negligible. Avoid applying to the breast/nipple area to prevent direct infant contact.
renal: Not applicable for topical cosmetic use. Systemic absorption is minimal and no renal dose adjustment concept applies.
hepatic: Not applicable for topical cosmetic use. Systemic absorption is minimal and no hepatic dose adjustment concept applies.

pearls: NOT FDA-approved as a drug: climbazole is a topical/cosmetic antifungal used mainly as an anti-dandruff active and cosmetic preservative; the information here is from non-FDA sources (EMA/SCCS - Scientific Committee on Consumer Safety - and cosmetic-ingredient assessments), not an FDA label
Typically used at around 0.5-2% in finished cosmetic formulations; permitted in-use concentrations differ for rinse-off versus leave-on products and are set by cosmetic safety regulation
Active against Malassezia (Pityrosporum) yeasts implicated in dandruff and seborrhoeic dermatitis
Often combined with other anti-dandruff actives (e.g. zinc pyrithione) in shampoos
There is no oral/systemic dosing; renal and hepatic adjustments are not applicable given minimal systemic absorption
missed: Not applicable in the conventional dosing sense - this is a topical cosmetic product. If a scheduled application (e.g. a wash) is missed, simply resume normal use at the next opportunity per the product directions; do not apply extra to compensate.
overdose: Systemic overdose is not expected from normal topical/cosmetic use due to minimal absorption. Excessive application may cause local scalp/skin irritation - rinse off and discontinue. Accidental ingestion should be managed with standard supportive care; contact a poison control centre or seek medical advice for significant ingestion.
